newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo precious metals end volatile session higher.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo precious metals end volatile session higher.

text.p: Yen-based Tokyo precious metal futures ended a volatile session higher, buoyed by firmer spot prices and the yen's slip, and the April and December silver contracts rose by their daily limit of six yen per 10 grams, traders said.
Gold futures ranged from 10 yen to 16 yen per gram higher. Most-active benchmark December ended up 14 yen at 1,340 yen.

"Heavy short-covering by funds in the bullion market before the Tokyo opening prompted TOCOM gold up from the outset. Prices maintained early gains, helped by the yen's further weakness," a senior dealer at a foreign bank said.
The dollar briefly skyrockted above 120 yen in late Tokyo trade on Friday, a fresh 47-month high.
Spot gold ended at $352.20/50 per ounce at the Tokyo close after rising to $354.00/300 during the Asian hours. The New York close on Thursday was $351.25/75.
Traders said the rebound in gold was led by gains in spot silver and falls in the U.S. stock market, but they said bearish sentiment in the longer-term remained intact.
In TOCOM gold futures, profit-taking by local investors above 1,340 yen levels capped gains, while trade houses bought futures and sold spot gold in arbitrage trade.

Silver futures were lifted by stronger spot silver prices, but individual investors who were buying earlier turned to take profits later in the day. Benchmark December rose by the daily limit of six yen per 10 grams to 186.2 yen.

Three distant palladium futures hit their life-of-contract highs as uncertainty over Japan-Russia talks supported the market. Selling in distant months by private investors were countered by trade house buying at TOCOM. Benchmark December palladium rose five yen to 462 yen. Benchmark December platinum was up 10 yen per gram at 1,356 yen.
